thesis: The single most valuable conversion mechanism on this site is the pricing page's ability to convert visitors into plan selections, but it is bleeding value because the page lacks a clear, plan-specific call-to-action and presents conflicting prices across the site, undermining trust and leaving visitors without a direct path to purchase.

findings.title: Competing CTAs on homepage
findings.summary: The homepage presents multiple equally prominent CTAs pointing to different destinations, making the primary next step ambiguous for new visitors.
findings.problem: The homepage presents multiple equally prominent CTAs pointing to different destinations, making the primary next step ambiguous for new visitors.
findings.recommended_change: cta: One primary CTA above the fold (e.g., Get Started Free); notes: Visually subordinate secondary links
findings.evidence: 11 distinct calls to action compete on the same page: “Contact Us We are here to help”, “Get Started Free”, “Find Your Seat”, “Contact Us”, “Explore RSVP Tool →”, “Explore Digital Seating Chart →”, “Explore Wedibox Embed →”, “Try Free Demo”.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 1.0-5.0% relative lift

findings.title: Missing trust signals above the fold
findings.summary: The homepage shows no sign of returns policy, guarantee, security badge, so a first-time visitor has nothing to offset purchase risk.
findings.problem: The homepage shows no sign of returns policy, guarantee, security badge, so a first-time visitor has nothing to offset purchase risk.
findings.recommended_change: notes: Surface review counts, the returns window and a guarantee near the primary call to action.
findings.evidence: Measured on the live homepage: no match for returns policy, guarantee, security badge.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 1.0-5.0% relative lift

findings.title: Unclear what $49 buys
findings.summary: The homepage lists a $49 price without stating which plan or features it corresponds to, leaving visitors uncertain about the offer above the fold.
findings.problem: The homepage lists a $49 price without stating which plan or features it corresponds to, leaving visitors uncertain about the offer above the fold.
findings.recommended_change: notes: Add line specifying which plan $49 refers to and what it includes
findings.evidence: Prices shown on the page: $49 $49 $49 | The page's main headline reads “One Wedding QR Code for Collecting Photos , Videos , Messages , Voicemails , RSVPs , and Seating ”.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 0.5-2.0% relative lift

findings.title: Lab Largest Contentful Paint of 3.5 s on mobile
findings.summary: Measured in a lab load: the page's main content takes this long to appear on a mid-range phone; most visitors have bounced long before.
findings.problem: Measured in a lab load: the page's main content takes this long to appear on a mid-range phone; most visitors have bounced long before.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse (mobile emulation, single synthetic run via DataForSEO): Largest Contentful Paint 3.5 s against a ‘good’ threshold of 2500ms. Lab data, not real-user field data — confirms the defect class, not the field percentile.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 0.5-2.0% relative lift

findings.title: Missing primary CTA on pricing page
findings.summary: The pricing page presents plans and prices but lacks a clear, plan-specific call-to-action, leaving visitors without a direct path to purchase.
findings.problem: The pricing page presents plans and prices but lacks a clear, plan-specific call-to-action, leaving visitors without a direct path to purchase.
findings.recommended_change: cta: Plan-specific primary CTA button beneath each pricing tier; notes: Leads to checkout or get-started flow
findings.evidence: 9 distinct calls to action compete on the same page: “Contact Us We are here to help”, “Get Started Free”, “Find Your Seat”, “Contact Us”, “Explore Embed”, “Start over”, “See supported platforms →”, “See how Wedibox works”.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 2.0-8.0% relative lift

findings.title: Inconsistent pricing across pages

findings.problem: The homepage and pricing page show conflicting price points for the same product, undermining clarity of cost.
